He continued to strengthen him until He made manifest in him the sign of His glory and made His religion prevail over every religion, and people entered it willingly and unwillingly, in ways of glory that are known to whoever recalls the biography, especially whoever knows the affair of the Banu Asad and Ghatafan, concerning whom these verses were revealed, and how their condition was in the expedition of Khaybar and elsewhere.

Since the purpose of this was to show their ignorance and to teach them the realities of matters, and not to testify to their guidance, He drew attention to that by saying: ﴿If you are﴾, that is, being those who are firmly established in it, ﴿truthful﴾ in your claim to that. For on the supposition of truthfulness, it is only by God's enabling, and it is He who created for you the power of obedience. So He is the real doer, and therefore the favour belongs to Him over you. Abu al-Qasim al-Qushayri said: Whoever observes any of his own deeds or states, if he sees them as other than himself, it is polytheism (*shirk*), and if he sees them as belonging to himself, it is deception (*makr*). How then can a servant confer a favour through what is polytheism or deception? And what is obligatory upon him is to accept the favour; how can he see for himself a favour over another? This, by my life, is a disgrace. And favour spoils the good deed when it comes from created beings, while through favour a blessing becomes pleasant when it comes from God.

When He negated from them what was hidden, and concluded His argument against them with this conditional clause, one of limited perception and rigid thought might have imagined that they lacked knowledge of what He is upon. He removed that (p-394) in a general manner and emphasized it, so He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the One who encompasses everything in power and knowledge, ﴿knows﴾, that is, by way of the affirmation of the attribute and the unrestricted continuity of its connection, whenever something new comes into being or is of a kind that comes into being, ﴿the unseen of the heavens﴾, that is, all of them, ﴿and the earth﴾, likewise.

Since generality was intended without restriction to the two horizons (al-khafiqayn), He made the Name explicit and did not use a pronoun, saying: ﴿And Allah﴾, that is, the One who has encompassing knowledge of that and of other things you do not know, ﴿is All-Seeing﴾, that is, the Knower with the most complete knowledge, outward and inward, ﴿of what you do﴾, of the outward of your Islam and the inward of your faith, in the past, the present and the future, whether it is apparent or hidden, whether it has occurred so that you know it, or whether it is implanted in your natures and hidden from you.

This is according to the reading with the second person, which is a shift (iltifat) toward them to rescue those among them who had this imagining, and it is more eloquent. According to Ibn Kathir's reading with the third person (bil-ghayb), it follows the first style, of what the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to convey to them. He, glory be to Him, knows who harbours faith in his inner self, who is disposed to disbelief, who dies in the state he is in, and who changes his condition by being distanced from Him or drawn to Him.

Al-Qushayri, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Whoever stops here, life becomes troubled for him, since he does not know what his unseen state holds for him." And in this meaning someone said:

*I weep, and do you know what makes me weep?
I weep out of fear that you will leave me,
and cut my rope and abandon me.*

End of quotation.

In this there is the greatest warning and intimidation for whoever puts himself forward before Allah and His Messenger, even if his putting forward is in his secret; for there is no threat more forceful than the encompassing of knowledge. It is as if it were said: "Do not put yourselves forward before Him, for Allah has all-encompassing knowledge; He knows your secret and your open speech." Thus this last part has returned to the first, and wrapped around it as the branch is wrapped around the root that connects it.
